sentiment.rationale: Guidance was raised materially: free cash flow guidance for 2026 is $6.5-$6.8 billion, which management explicitly states is 'well above our prior expectation' (Evan Scott). Additionally, segment operating profit growth is guided to 'more than 25%' year-over-year, and sales growth of approximately 5% is expected. The guidance raise is organic, driven by production ramps and new multi-year framework agreements, not attributed to one-time items. Management language is highly confident, with CEO Jim Taiclet stating 'we are well positioned to perform' and 'this notable start to 2026 reinforces our confidence.'

summary.revenue: Full year 2025 sales of $75.0 billion, up 6% year-over-year. Q4 2025 sales of $20.3 billion, up 9% year-over-year.
summary.eps: Full year 2025 diluted EPS of $21.49, down 4% from $22.31 in 2024. Q4 2025 diluted EPS of $5.80, up from $2.22 in Q4 2024.
summary.guidance: 2026 outlook: Sales $77.5-$80.0 billion (midpoint ~5% growth), segment operating profit $8.425-$8.675 billion (midpoint margin 10.9%), diluted EPS $29.35-$30.25, free cash flow $6.5-$6.8 billion (well above prior expectation).
summary.margin: Full year 2025 consolidated operating margin 10.3% (up from 9.9% in 2024). Segment operating profit margin 9.0% (up from 8.6% in 2024). Q4 2025 consolidated operating margin 11.5% (up from 3.7% in Q4 2024).
key_risks: Risk remains on Aeronautics classified programs: 'risk is gonna remain over the next few years' (Jim Taiclet in Q&A).
Earnings per share declined 4% year-over-year in 2025 due to increased interest expense, higher tax rate, and higher operating FAS/CAS expense.
RMS full-year segment operating profit declined 31% due to $610 million decrease in profit booking rate adjustments from charges on CMHP and TUHP.
Pension funding requirement returns in 2027 of at least $1 billion (Evan Scott in Q&A).
MFC margins may face 20-30 basis points dilution in early years of multi-year agreements (Evan Scott in Q&A).
key_opportunities: Record backlog of $194 billion, up 17% year-over-year, providing multi-year visibility.
Multi-year framework agreements for PAC-3 MSE and THAAD expected to triple annual production capacity from 600 to 2,000 units.
MFC sales expected to grow 14% in 2026, with line of sight to double-digit CAGR through end of decade (Evan Scott).
F-35 program: $15 billion in awards in Q4, additional $1 billion strategic investment in sustainment.
Space: $1 billion+ contract for 18 Tranche 3 Tracking Layer satellites.
Capital and R&D investment increasing ~35% to approach $5 billion in 2026, a 'step function increase' (Evan Scott).
